This also implies the existence of at least one victim and at least one danger. So, we need existential quantifiers for victims (∃y)Vy and danger (∃z)Dz. The predicate Rxyz means 'x rescues y from z', where x is the firefighter, y is the victim, and z is the danger. Combining these, we get: (∃x){Fx • (∃y)[Vy • (∃z)(Dz • Rxyz)]}. B) (∃x){Fx • (∃y)[Vy • (∃z)(Dz • Rxyz)]} - This translates to 'There exists a firefighter (x) such that x is a firefighter AND there exists a victim (y) such that y is a victim AND there exists a danger (z) such that z is a danger AND x rescues y from z.' This accurately captures the meaning of the original sentence.
C) (∃x){Fx • (∃y)(∃z)[(Vy • Dz) • Rxzy]} - The predicate is Rxzy, which means 'x rescues z from y'. The problem states Rxyz means 'x rescues y from z'. So, the order of y and z is incorrect.
D) (∀x){Fx ⊃ (∃y)[Vy . (∃z)(Dz • Rxyz)]} - This translates to 'For all firefighters, there exists a victim and a danger such that the firefighter rescues the victim from the danger.' This means 'All firefighters rescue victims from danger,' which is not what 'Some firefighters' implies.
